question: Is the sigma_theta_teos10 bound (-8 to 37 kg m-3) acceptable? It is derived, not observed: gsw_sigma0 over a 1-unit grid spanning the registered bottle temperature (-2 to 40 deg C) and salinity (0 to 45 PSS-78) bounds at 0 dbar, rounded outward.
context: A bound must describe what is physically possible, never the observed range. The derivation is in the ingest's register-types chunk. spiciness0 reuses the bound calcofi_ctd-derived declared (its Q07), which covers the same grid. Observed at the first render (2026-10-20, input release v2026.10.19): sigma_theta_teos10 16.998 to 28.152, spiciness0 -5.655 to 7.266 over 842,591 bottles; the low ends are cruise 2021-05-3322 (Q03).
proposed_answer: valid_min -8, valid_max 37 (derived from the registered bottle T/S bounds)

label: Q03
question: The TEOS-10 sigma-theta differs from the bottle database's own (DECODR) sigma_theta by more than 0.1 kg m-3 on 928 bottles. On 918 of them, every bottle of cruise 2021-05-3322, Salnty equals the bottle's own sigma_theta to 0.01 (24.19-27.06), so the salinity column carries sigma-theta (calcofi_bottle Q13), and the spice (-5.7 to -3) and TEOS-10 sigma-theta (17.0-21) computed from it are not real. The other 10 (2005-07-32NM, 2008-01-31JD x5, 2014-04-32I1, 2020-01-33UD, 2020-07-33P4 x2) differ by 0.105-0.786: was the legacy value computed from a different salinity or temperature than the one published?
context: Measured at the first render (2026-10-20, input release v2026.10.19) over 840,508 bottles with both values and an unflagged legacy sigma_theta: median |difference| 0.0041 kg m-3, p95 0.0109, p99 0.0154, max 7.20; 53,712 bottles differ by more than 0.01. Spice below -3 kg m-3: 918 bottles, all on 2021-05-3322. The per-bottle list is in the ingest's Findings section. These values are inside the generous bounds and unflagged in the source (S_qual above 9 is blanked as good by calcofi_bottle Q01), so nothing is deleted here; the dataset follows calcofi_bottle Q13 for 2021-05-3322.
proposed_answer: 2021-05-3322: once calcofi_bottle Q13 is answered (salinity invalid, or re-scaled), the next render of calcofi_bottle and of this dataset follows it. The 10 others: the legacy value stays as published (DECODR's record) and the TEOS-10 value is computed from the published temperature and salinity; flag the bottle's salinity or temperature if it is the wrong input.

question: Is T_degC in the bottle database on the ITS-90 temperature scale throughout, including the bottles before 1990 (IPTS-68)? gsw_CT_from_t expects ITS-90.
context: The two scales differ by about 0.00024 x T (0.007 deg C at 30 deg C, under 0.005 deg C in most CalCOFI water), which moves sigma_theta_teos10 by under 0.002 kg/m3 and spice by a similar amount: below the bottle's own reporting precision. The derivation takes T_degC as ITS-90 for every year.
proposed_answer: treat T_degC as ITS-90 for every year (no conversion); the effect is below the bottle's precision
